name: Champaran Mutton (Ahuna Meat)
instructions: 1. In a large bowl, mix the mutton with sliced onions, ginger-garlic paste, all powdered spices, salt, and raw mustard oil until well coated.
2. Add the whole garlic bulbs, dried red chillies, and whole spices to the mixture.
3. Heat a small amount of mustard oil and coat the inside of a clay pot (handi).
4. Transfer the marinated mutton into the clay pot and cover the opening with a piece of dough (atta) to seal it airtight with the lid.
5. Cook the pot over low heat (traditionally coal or wood fire) for about 60 to 90 minutes.
6. Shake the pot periodically to prevent sticking.
7. Once cooked, open the seal and serve hot with litti or steamed rice.
description: Champaran Mutton, also known as Ahuna Meat or Handi Meat, originates from the Champaran district of Bihar. It is a traditional culinary masterpiece characterized by the earthy aroma imparted by cooking in clay pots over charcoal. Historically, it was a celebratory meal for travelers and locals alike, representing the authentic, slow-living spirit of Bihari cuisine.
